name: web-read
description: Reading a page off the internet. Four cases chosen so the differences between these tools are visible rather than asserted: a static page everything should manage; a page whose content only exists after JavaScript runs; a page that answers 403 to an obvious robot; and a real article with navigation, sidebars and footers around it, where `absent` is the boilerplate check. A tool that is not installed here is reported as unavailable and kept out of the totals — not set up is not the same as worse.

cases.about: The floor. Anything that cannot do this is broken, not slow.
The quotes are rendered by a script. A plain GET sees the shell and nothing in it; only a real browser sees the quotes.

A real page with navigation, sidebars and footers around the text. The `contains` proves the article arrived; the `absent` entries are Wikipedia's chrome, so a tool that passes both is extracting the article rather than the page.
